speaker: YOU
text: Right now, you're spinning at up to one thousand miles an hour.

speaker: YOU
text: You can't feel it... but the whole planet is turning under your feet.

speaker: YOU
text: So what if Earth stopped spinning... for just one second?

speaker: YOU
text: I know exactly what happens. Because I was there when it did.

speaker: YOU
text: It all started the day I flew to the North Pole.

speaker: FRIEND
text: The North Pole? Bro, what are you gonna do up there, help Santa wrap presents?

speaker: YOU
text: My uncle runs a science camp on the ice. I won a spot to visit for a week.

speaker: FRIEND
text: Whatever. I'm flying to my grandma's house tomorrow. At least she has Wi-Fi.

speaker: YOU
text: Everyone laughed at my trip. Nobody's laughing now.

speaker: UNCLE
text: Want to see something crazy? Stand right here.

speaker: UNCLE
text: You're standing on top of the world. The exact spot the Earth spins around.

speaker: UNCLE
text: At the equator, the ground is moving a thousand miles an hour. Faster than a jet.

speaker: UNCLE
text: But up here? You're just turning in a slow little circle. One spin every twenty-four hours.

speaker: YOU
text: So I'm the slowest person on Earth?

speaker: UNCLE
text: Technically... yes.

speaker: YOU
text: Cool. I didn't think it would ever matter.

speaker: YOU
text: The next day, at exactly 3:14 p.m.... Earth stopped.

speaker: YOU
text: Just for one second.

speaker: YOU
text: But here's the problem. The ground stopped. Nothing else did.

speaker: YOU
text: It's like when a bus slams on the brakes. Everything inside keeps going.

speaker: YOU
text: Except this bus was the size of a planet.

speaker: YOU
text: Cars, oceans, the air, people... everything that wasn't bolted down kept flying east at up to a thousand miles an hour.

speaker: YOU
text: Faster than the speed of sound.

speaker: YOU
text: The air hit first. Winds four times faster than the strongest gust ever recorded.

speaker: YOU
text: Sonic booms cracked windows in every city on the planet.

speaker: YOU
text: Then the oceans. Trillions of tons of water kept rushing east and slammed into the coastlines.

speaker: YOU
text: Waves taller than skyscrapers.

speaker: YOU
text: Buildings are bolted to the ground, so they stopped... but everything inside them didn't.

speaker: YOU
text: And all of that happened in one second.

speaker: YOU
text: Then... Earth started spinning again.

speaker: UNCLE
text: Here's the weird part. Everything that was flying east... the ground just caught back up to it.

speaker: YOU
text: So it stopped being a disaster?

speaker: UNCLE
text: No. The damage was already done. One second was enough.

speaker: YOU
text: And up at the North Pole? I felt a little bump. My hot chocolate spilled.

speaker: YOU
text: That was it.

speaker: UNCLE
text: Up here, the ground was barely moving to begin with. So when it stopped... there was nothing to stop.

speaker: YOU
text: But all I could think about was Jake. He was supposed to be flying that day.

speaker: YOU
text: I called him fifty times. Nothing.

speaker: YOU
text: Then, at midnight... my phone rang.

speaker: FRIEND
text: Bro! Our plane hit the craziest turbulence ever!

speaker: YOU
text: Wait... you were in the air when it happened?

speaker: UNCLE
text: Of course! A plane flies inside the air. When Earth stopped, the air kept moving... and so did the plane.

speaker: FRIEND
text: Also, my grandma says she's never flying again.

speaker: YOU
text: So the two safest places on Earth when it stopped spinning? The top of the world... and the sky.

speaker: YOU
text: And the craziest part? Earth really is slowing down. Every day gets a tiny bit longer.

speaker: UNCLE
text: About two milliseconds every century.

speaker: YOU
text: So don't worry. You've got a few billion years.

speaker: YOU
text: But if it ever happens... I know where I'm going.
